title: 1 Rook VS 2 Pawns
reviewNotes: Four branches and 19 checked positions from the complete five-piece opening. Corrected the source premature-king example: Kf7 draws, ...d3 returns a White win, Ra4 returns a draw. Added independent ...e2 drawing defense. Rh2+ is not actual mate: the sole ...Qh4 interposition is followed by independently supplied Rxh4#. Source winning plan remains valid.
transcript: How can the white rook stop the two pawns? You see, there is a rule in chess that says that once two pawns are connected and only two steps away from getting a new queen, even a rook cannot stop them. And we can test that. If the rook goes behind this pawn, now it's going to push and be defended by the other pawn. Of course, we cannot go after this pawn or this one is going to promote. But if we play a move like, for example, rook to D3, now black can actually push because you cannot stop both of these promotions at the same time. But you might notice that there is a possibility of attacking this king. So, if we go back to the start of this position, we could come up with the idea of playing king to F7 and now trap the black king and possibly threaten a checkmate in the future. But after black pushes the pawn, we realize that this is not enough. White can threaten the checkmate like this, but black is always going to be able to just move the king and create a new escape square. So, at best, we have a draw by keep repeating this pattern. We create a checkmate threat and black creates an escape. There is no continuation. But you see, chess and life are very similar. Sometimes what seems obvious and very simple it's not as good as the hardest path. And indeed, in this position, the only way for white to win this game is to play the very counterintuitive king to E7, not getting closer to the black king quite yet and seemingly allowing black to get an extra move for free. But patience is the virtue of the strong. And white now plays king to F7, seemingly creating the same exact position except that this time black is only one step away from getting a new queen. Of course, white cannot allow that and has to stop the promotion. But we saw that black can push the other pawn and we said we cannot stop both promotions at the same time. But you see, we actually wanted black to be closer to promotion. Because now, after the deep pawn falls, either black moves the king and loses his last pawn or after the black pawn promotes, [music] black is paving the way for the rook to come in and deliver checkmate.
